Multiplier-resampling (MR) inference quantities as a tidy data frame

Source: R/mr_values.R
mr_values.Rd

Extracts the MR quantities of a forestsearch() fit (its mr_inference element) or of a bare fs_mr_inference() result into a plain data frame, one row per region: "H" (the selected subgroup) and, when the complement block exists, "Hc" (its complement). This is pure extraction: every value already exists in mr_inference and nothing is recomputed, apart from the optional log() of scale = "log".

Usage

mr_values(x, scale = c("effect", "log"))

Arguments

x

A forestsearch() fit with a non-NULL mr_inference element, or the list returned by fs_mr_inference() (including its short variant, which yields an "H" row that is NA apart from n_family).

scale

"effect" (the default) returns every column exactly as stored. "log" applies log() to the columns listed as effect scale below, for ratio measures (HR, OR, RR, IRR); it is an error for identity measures (MD, RD). The other columns are returned as stored under both settings.

Value

A plain data.frame with a fixed set of columns, whatever the fit computed: a quantity the fit did not compute is NA, and no column is ever dropped. The "Hc" row is present whenever complement is non-NULL; if the complement could not be fit, that row is all NA. Below, working scale means log for ratio measures and the effect itself for identity measures. Paths are relative to mr_inference.

  • row: "H" or "Hc".

  • n: Patients in the region: n_selected on "H", complement$n on "Hc". Count. NA in the short return, or when the complement could not be fit.

  • naive_est, naive_lower, naive_upper: The unadjusted estimate with its two-sided 95% robust interval: naive$est, naive$lower, naive$upper, and complement$naive on "Hc". Effect scale. NA in the short return, or when the complement could not be fit.

  • debiased_est: The two-term de-biased estimate: debiased$est, and complement$debiased$est on "Hc". Effect scale. NA as naive_est.

  • ij_lower, ij_upper: The two-sided 95% two-term IJ interval: debiased$lower, debiased$upper, and complement$debiased on "Hc". Effect scale. Also NA under ci_method = "wald" or ij_residual != "two_term", when those two stored limits are not this interval.

  • ij_se: The two-term IJ standard error: debiased$se_ij_two_term, and complement$debiased$se_ij_two_term on "Hc". Working scale, under both settings of scale. It is the subgroup robust SE when the IJ variance is unusable (debiased$ij_source is "wald_fallback"). NA as naive_est.

  • field_est2: The field second-order point estimate: field$est2, and field$complement$est2 on "Hc". Effect scale. NA unless ci_method = "field", and on "Hc" unless the complement field ran (field_complement = TRUE with include_complement = TRUE), or when that block returned a note instead of numbers.

  • field_est2_s: The studentized field-s counterpart on "Hc": field$complement$est2_s. Effect scale. NA on "H", and on "Hc" as field_est2 or under field_scale_complement = "none".

  • field_lower_1s: The field one-sided 95% lower bound on "H": field$lower_1s. Effect scale. NA on "Hc", and unless ci_method = "field".

  • field_upper_1s: The field one-sided 95% upper bound on "Hc": field$complement$upper_1s. Effect scale. NA on "H", and on "Hc" as field_est2.

  • field_upper_1s_s: The field-s one-sided 95% upper bound on "Hc": field$complement$upper_1s_s. Effect scale. NA as field_est2_s.

  • bonf_lower_H, bonf_upper_Hc: The Bonferroni pair (each bound at 97.5%, jointly 95%), from the field's joint block: field$joint$bonf_lower_H on "H", field$joint$bonf_upper_Hc on "Hc". Effect scale. NA on the other row, and when field$joint is absent, which it is unless the complement field ran, or has no bounds.

  • bonf_lower_H_s, bonf_upper_Hc_s: The same pair from the field-s joint block, field$joint_s. Effect scale. NA on the other row, and when field$joint_s is absent, as for bonf_lower_H, or under field_scale_complement = "none".

  • selection_bias: The selection-bias term: selection_bias. Working scale, under both settings of scale. Fit-level: "H" row only. NA in the short return.

  • p_hat: The selected candidate's re-selection frequency: reselection$p_hat[[selected_index]]. A probability. "H" row only. NA under return_reselection = FALSE, or in the short return.

  • n_family: The candidate family's size: n_family. Count. "H" row only.

  • n_selected: Patients in the selected subgroup: n_selected. Count. "H" row only. NA in the short return.

  • timing_seconds: Seconds in the main multiplier stage: timing_seconds. "H" row only. NA in the short return.

  • field_timing_seconds: Seconds in the field block: field$timing_seconds. "H" row only. NA unless ci_method = "field".

  • field_complement_timing_seconds: Seconds in the complement field block: field$complement$timing_seconds. "H" row only. NA as field_est2 on "Hc".

Details

Only the evaluated construction set is exposed: the naive estimate, the two-term infinitesimal-jackknife (IJ) de-biased estimate, the field one-sided bounds (lower on the selected subgroup, upper on its complement, plain and studentized) and the Bonferroni pair, with the fit-level diagnostics.

See also

forestsearch() for the mr_inference switch; fs_mr_inference() for the computation; mr_estimates_table() to render the estimates as a table.

Examples

set.seed(11)
n <- 300
d <- data.frame(time = rexp(n, 0.2), event = rbinom(n, 1, 0.8),
                treat = rbinom(n, 1, 0.5), x1 = rnorm(n), x2 = rnorm(n))
family <- list(g1 = which(d$x1 > 0), g2 = which(d$x2 > 0),
               g3 = which(d$x1 + d$x2 > 0.3))
spec <- list(outcome_type = "survival", effect_measure = "HR",
             treat.name = "treat", outcome.name = "time",
             event.name = "event", offset.name = NULL,
             adjust_covariates = NULL, adverse_outcome = TRUE)
fit <- fs_mr_inference(
  df = d, candidates = family, spec = spec,
  selected_members = family$g1,
  admission = list(effect_floor = NULL, consistency = NULL),
  reselection = "maxeff", draws = 300L, seed = 4242L,
  ci_method = "field", include_complement = TRUE,
  field_R_out = 200L, field_R_in = 50L)
mr_values(fit)
#>   row   n naive_est naive_lower naive_upper debiased_est  ij_lower ij_upper
#> 1   H 151 0.9279521   0.6438566    1.337402    0.8627701 0.4005693 1.858286
#> 2  Hc 149 0.7760111   0.5378543    1.119621    0.8694547 0.4515283 1.674206
#>       ij_se field_est2 field_est2_s field_lower_1s field_upper_1s
#> 1 0.3914672  0.8563254           NA      0.6222182             NA
#> 2 0.3343062  0.9039651    0.9050143             NA       1.230306
#>   field_upper_1s_s bonf_lower_H bonf_upper_Hc bonf_lower_H_s bonf_upper_Hc_s
#> 1               NA    0.5935985            NA      0.5935985              NA
#> 2         1.230768           NA      1.416401             NA        1.408442
#>   selection_bias p_hat n_family n_selected timing_seconds field_timing_seconds
#> 1     0.07958234  0.46        3        151          0.005                0.031
#> 2             NA    NA       NA         NA             NA                   NA
#>   field_complement_timing_seconds
#> 1                           0.019
#> 2                              NA
mr_values(fit, scale = "log")[, c("row", "naive_est", "ij_se", "selection_bias")]
#>   row  naive_est     ij_se selection_bias
#> 1   H -0.0747752 0.3914672     0.07958234
#> 2  Hc -0.2535885 0.3343062             NA
